label: prop:ice-pauling-residual
title: Pauling residual entropy of ice: $W_1 = 3/2$
html:
Proposition. Pauling residual entropy of ice: W_1 = 3/2

Proposition (Pauling residual entropy of ice). In ice I_h each water molecule is hydrogen-bonded to four neighbours — two as donor (its two H's) and two as acceptor (its two lone pairs), the four directions of the H_2O braid. Subject to the ice rule that every bond carries exactly one hydrogen, the per-molecule multiplicity is

 W_1 \;=\; \binom{4}{2}\left(\tfrac12\right)^{2} \;=\; \frac{6}{4} \;=\; \frac{3}{2},

thus the molar residual entropy is S = R\ln\tfrac32 \approx 3.37\ \mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}} (Pauling, 1935). This agrees closely with the measured ice calorimetry.
